title: GENESIS / How GENESIS works
heading: How GENESIS works
text: How GENESIS works The GENESIS Context Engine turns world memory, settings and player actions into model context. An external LLM creates prompts and structured replies. Your World Model generates the scene, streaming delivery brings it to the interface, and the next action continues the loop. Visual Context is an optional part of the GENESIS Context Engine. It uses world settings and LLM prompts to prepare starting or reference images, then sends image context directly to the World Model alongside text context. Scroll the diagram horizontally to explore the full loop. GENESIS prepares text and visual context. Connect your LLM and World Model through replaceable adapters; your host supplies credentials, generation services and streaming delivery. Explore the architecture .

title: GENESIS / What GENESIS handles
heading: What GENESIS handles
text: What GENESIS handles You define the experience. GENESIS runs the state and interaction loop around your connected models. Context Engine Combine world memory, settings and accepted actions into context for your connected models. World memory Remember choices, quest progress and relationships from one turn to the next. Inventory and variables Track items, health, scores and resources using your world's rules. Characters and locations Keep your cast, places and scene facts organized for the next generation request. LLM prompts and replies Pass world context to your LLM and validate structured moves, dialogue and choices. Visual Context Optionally create starting or reference images from world settings and LLM prompts, then supply image context to your World Model. Custom interfaces Build player controls, inventory panels and overlays with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Multiplayer and shared rules Coordinate player seats, turns and crowd votes. Keep everyone's accepted state in sync. Scene continuity Track generation jobs, carry the actual last frame forward and advance after playback. Portable worlds and assets Export your settings, interface, controller and declared media in one complete bundle.

title: GENESIS / What can you build?
heading: What can you build?
text: What can you build? One engine, many kinds of infinite experience. Start with a world people can play, watch, explore or learn from. Play Games, multiplayer games and creative sandboxes. Build quests, cooperative battles and worlds players can keep changing. Watch Infinite TV, interactive stories and live events. Create ongoing shows and performances shaped by the audience. Explore Travel experiences, social worlds and virtual showrooms. Visit destinations, meet characters and tour spaces together. Learn Learning experiences, interactive history lessons and robotics training simulations. Practice languages, step into another era or connect specialist simulation tools. Practice Coaching, training and rehearsal, and therapy and wellbeing. Rehearse interviews and workplace scenarios, or build practitioner-led reflection experiences. You supply the domain content, rules and any specialist tools your experience needs.

title: Quickstart with the Genesis skill / Skill reference
heading: Skill reference
text: Skill reference The skill ships with the Apache 2.0 licensed engine. Download SKILL.md , or expand the full instructions below. Read the full authoring instructions Turn the user's idea into a working world, a local preview and a validated exportable bundle. Choose mechanics, presentation and reasonable defaults from the prompt. Ask only for information that blocks the requested behavior. Preserve the user's chosen provider and existing world behavior. Sequencer is the default managed integration when a provider has not been chosen. Read the package's README and docs/api.md. Use genesis init with the nearest template, then implement the requested world in genesis.json, interface.html and controller.js. Adapt the actual controls, rules and scene context to the idea. Use the local runner's labeled fixtures for an immediate preview; connect live generation when the provider is configured and spending is authorized. The stock local runner returns the arena move fixture for LLM requests. For a different responseSchema, supply matching fixture data through a local host provider using createLlmProvider; keep preview-only providers outside the portable project. Do not present a fixture response as live generation. Use window.Genesis for browser actions, state subscriptions, seats and assets. Read actor eligibility from the accepted host view. Keep health, turn order, vote outcomes and permitted state transitions in synchronous onEvent(context) . Render LLM names as text; never evaluate model output as HTML or JavaScript. For generated moves or world choices, request tool.llm.genera

title: World memory
heading: World memory, inventory and characters
text: World memory, inventory and characters A World Model receives the context for its next scene. GENESIS stores the facts that make that scene part of the same experience: what players carry, where they are, who they met and which decisions changed the world. Define your world's facts The controller state is JSON. Choose the structure that fits your world. For example: Copy { "location": "mosslight_gate", "inventory": ["brass_key", "healing_herb"], "health": 90, "quests": {"find_the_lighthouse": "active"}, "locations": { "mosslight_gate": {"visited": true, "doorUnlocked": false} }, "characters": { "keeper": {"name": "Mira", "relationship": "trusted"} } } This is an example state shape. Your controller defines the inventory rules, character behavior, location transitions and values your interface displays. Public, private and server state State Use it for public Shared inventory, visible characters, location and game progress. private A participant's hidden information. The host filters the view by actor. server Internal encounter IDs, generation guards and facts the controller needs to keep off the public view. The host persists accepted state with the session. Memory and file adapters support one host process; production hosts choose storage for their deployment. This preview bounds session state to 200 KB. Long histories and external memory stores belong in host adapters. Resolv

title: World memory / Resolve the action first
heading: Resolve the action first
text: Resolve the action first When a player uses the brass key, the controller checks the accepted inventory and current location. It commits the unlocked door to state, then requests a scene describing that outcome. The interface submits a declared, typed action. The host checks actor eligibility and the current input window. The controller commits the inventory and location changes. A bounded backend request carries the outcome and relevant world context. Validated results return to the controller and update the accepted view. The LLM can describe a character's response or propose structured choices. Your rules remain the authority for inventory, health, access and turn order.

title: World memory / Keep generated data structured
heading: Keep generated data structured
text: Keep generated data structured For generated moves, dialogue or choices, use tool.llm.generate with a bounded object response schema. Choose fields such as name, description and permitted numeric attributes. Render model text as text in the interface. Use an encounter or scene guard so an old LLM result cannot replace the current decision. The arena-llm starter generates four moves once per encounter. See structured LLM helpers .

title: World memory / Give the next scene the right context
heading: Give the next scene the right context
text: Give the next scene the right context Scene requests can carry intent, a required outcome, an anchor and a spending ceiling. Include the facts that matter for this scene rather than sending every stored detail. Carry the actual decoded end frame into the next video request. Generation completion and playback completion are separate events. Reopen visual actions after the host accepts playback completion. GENESIS keeps the state and job lifecycle consistent. Visual fidelity depends on the connected World Model. Read the controller API and architecture .

heading: Publish your world on Sequencer
text: Publish your world on Sequencer Open My Worlds with your Sequencer account. Create a world and import your GENESIS project in the editor, or ask Spark to build it from a prompt. Preview the world, save it and publish it to Worldstreams. The hosted editor uses your existing identity, workspace, media library and gems. The API workflow below uses a server-side key for creators building in their own tools. Browser imports use the existing signed-in session. Use createLlmProvider with a generate(request, context) callback and a durable result store for paid calls. The request contains prompt, optional context and a bounded JSON responseSchema. The callback receives sessionId, a stable idempotencyKey and maxCostUsd. Keep the provider key on your server. The adapter validates output and sends it as job.ready's event.data.data. Paid providers must enforce the cost ceiling before submission. In-process deduplication does not replace distributed locks. createSequencerLlmProvider connects that callback to the Sequencer LLM endpoint. FileGenesisToolResults is an atomic single-host store. Configure a transaction-backed result store for distributed workers. Keep the world generation adapter separate from the LLM adapter so either can be replaced. Image/audio/video generation uses SequencerClient.generate; enumerate supported models with models(), inspect model(modelId), pass a cost ceiling and retain the returned media/job ID. Read status and completed media through media(workspaceId, mediaId). A thumbnail is not an actual video end-frame checkpoint. SequencerClient.save uploads declare

title: Your own models
heading: Provider integration
text: Provider integration A provider is a host module. Projects submit semantic effects and never receive provider credentials. Register providers and allowed capabilities when creating GenesisHost. Paid providers require services.authorizeTool, even when the creator requests access in the manifest. Prepared media createCachedProvider([{videoUrl,imageUrl}]) exercises queue, completion, playback and checkpoints with owned prepared assets. The image must represent the clip's actual last frame. Starter assets are included for no-cost local development. Replicate createReplicateProvider takes a server token and a host-registered model map. Each entry pins a 64-character version hash, provides maxEstimatedCostUsd, maps the Genesis job to model-specific inputs, and persists returned media through an asynchronous result callback. The callback must produce an immutable imageUrl for the actual final frame of scene videos. decodeGenesisEndFrame(inputPath,outputPath) handles bounded owned local files when ffmpeg/ffprobe are installed. See https://replicate.com/docs/reference/http for the provider protocol. Model costs are estimates, not a guaranteed external spending cap. title: Your own models / Replicate
heading: Replicate
text: Replicate createReplicateProvider takes a server token and a host-registered model map. Each entry pins a 64-character version hash, provides maxEstimatedCostUsd, maps the Genesis job to model-specific inputs, and persists returned media through an asynchronous result callback. The callback must produce an immutable imageUrl for the actual final frame of scene videos. decodeGenesisEndFrame(inputPath,outputPath) handles bounded owned local files when ffmpeg/ffprobe are installed. The adapter uses POST /v1/predictions, GET /v1/predictions/{id}, and POST /v1/predictions/{id}/cancel. Requests use Bearer authentication. See https://replicate.com/docs/reference/http for the provider protocol. Model costs are estimates, not a guaranteed external spending cap. Hosts enforce admission and actual billing through their own services and provider account controls. No creator price controls are introduced. Retry behavior depends on provider idempotency support. Replicate submission is deduplicated within the adapter process; uncertain submissions after process loss require reconciliation before a new attempt. The reference host does not automatically resubmit them. Output storage and remote downloading are host responsibilities. Allowlist provider/storage domains, validate redirects, bound download size and duration, and retain immutable assets. Do not let creator URLs become unrestricted server fetch targets. Protocol tests run without secrets. A deployment must test its chosen model's input mapping, output persistence and generation fidelity with live media before production use.

title: Your own models / Custom services
heading: Custom services
text: Custom services A provider can declare tool.audio.speak or tool.maps.lookup alongside its own argument validator and server implementation. Controllers request tool.request with toolId and data. Grant tool IDs independently in host policy. Return bounded result.data; the controller chooses what to expose to participants. Generic tool completion does not automatically replace the video stage. Uncertain paid submissions block participant retry. An operator can reconcile an existing prediction with host.reconcileProviderJob(jobId,providerId,predictionId). Restrict this to authenticated operator infrastructure. GenesisProviderSubmissionError(message,false) identifies a confirmed rejected submission; other paid start failures remain uncertain. This prevents automatic repeat charges after ambiguous network failures.

title: Models and pricing / Read the prices correctly
heading: Read the prices correctly
text: Read the prices correctly Sequencer: Advertises $40 per active stream hour. The session quote is authoritative. Viva includes built-in LLM world direction. Custom Genesis LLM requests and extra image/audio generation are separately metered. Worldstreams API , Genesis integration . fal H3 Max Director: Bills generated video, with a 60-second minimum. Public sessions currently have a 15-minute ceiling. Director pricing and session limits . Reactor: Bills wall-clock time while a session holds a GPU, including ready-but-idle time and recoverable disconnects. Use the session quote to confirm the applicable rate. Billing rules , current pricing API . The planned Orbis Stable route is estimated at $40.16 per session hour. Viva is $40 per active stream hour, with built-in LLM direction. title: Models and pricing / Read the timing correctly
heading: Read the timing correctly
text: Read the timing correctly Startup latency is the time from requesting a session to seeing its first usable frame. Response latency is the time from sending an action to seeing its effect. Generation speed describes how quickly video is produced. Chunk duration describes when a streaming model can accept a new direction. The timing column reports the measure each provider publishes. It is not a common end-to-end latency benchmark. Queuing, network delivery, buffering and your controller can change the wait a player experiences.

title: Models and pricing / Quality ratings
heading: Quality ratings
text: Quality ratings GENESIS uses a 1–5 rating for each of five criteria. The overall quality score is their mean, shown to one decimal place. Speed and price are reported separately. Criterion What to check Visual detail Clear subjects, readable environments and visible artifacts. Prompt adherence Whether the requested action, setting and constraints appear. Character consistency Whether identities, clothing and objects remain recognizable. Scene continuity Whether locations, spatial relationships and previous events carry forward. Motion and stability Natural movement, temporal consistency and recovery after a direction change. Use 1 for major failures, 2 for frequent failures, 3 for a usable result, 4 for a consistently strong result and 5 for a reliably excellent result across the test set. Score at least ten shared scenarios, run each three times for two minutes, and publish the prompts, model/version, resolution, settings, date and recordings. Include the same character, inventory and scene-transition challenges for every model. Have at least two reviewers score recordings without provider labels. No matched GENESIS benchmark has been completed. Every model is currently unrated , including Sequencer. A provider's demo or a clip-generation leaderboard does not establish its score for a persistent interactive world.

title: Models and pricing / Latency and moderation
heading: Latency and moderation
text: Latency and moderation First-token latency measures the wait before the first token arrives. Generation speed measures tokens produced per second after generation begins. Structured JSON usually needs to finish and pass validation before GENESIS can apply it. None of the listed services has a matched GENESIS end-to-end latency benchmark. The moderation column describes the controls we can verify. Google exposes adjustable filters alongside persistent core protections. Groq documents a separate moderation workflow. Open-weight models can have learned refusals, and hosted providers still apply their policies. A self-hosted app can choose whether to add a moderation layer; that does not remove refusals built into its chosen model. Google Gemini pricing and Flash-Lite model details support the token rates and low-latency design. Safety settings describe adjustable filters and core protections. Groq model catalog lists GPT OSS 20B at about 1,000 tokens/second. Content moderation describes an app moderation workflow. Cerebras pricing documents provider billing. Its model catalog lists about 3,000 tokens/second. Model and capacity availability can change. Provider speeds are published throughput claims, not measured GENESIS latency guarantees. Connect through Sequencer or bring your own adapter .

The shared API overview lists a different raster, so confirm the selected deployment's output before choosing it for resolution-sensitive work. title: SDK API reference

title: SDK API reference / Controller
heading: Controller
text: Controller Define classic JavaScript function onEvent(context) . The context includes state {public, private, server, window}, event {id,type,actorId?,actionId?,data,now}, participants, a server-only ballots snapshot, stage, anchors and config. It contains no host credential or wallet objects. Return an object with optional public/private/server state, window and effects. State updates replace their corresponding object. A window declares id, actionIds, mode (individual or collective), optional actorIds, choices and deadline. An empty actorIds array grants no actor permission. Collective windows require 2 to 12 choices. Window IDs must change between decisions. Choice and ballot payloads carry optionId; the browser SDK includes the current collective windowId. Events include session.started, participant.joined, participant.left, action, vote.cast, vote.resolved, vote.empty, timer, job.ready, job.failed, job.skipped and playback.completed. Generation completion describes prepared media. Playback completion means the host's participant policy has been satisfied. Effects: scene.request, image.request, live.direction, tool.request, stage.show, stage.restore, stage.play and timer.set. Each has a unique id. Tool effects carry intent, optional anchorId, modelId, duration, requiredOutcome and maxCostUsd. Timers carry delayMs and data. Stage play carries a saved videoUrl. A restored anchor preserves controller scores and inventory. Tools must be requested in the manifest and granted by the host. Stream defaults do not restrict operations in custom controllers. A provider still must

title: SDK API reference / Browser SDK
heading: Browser SDK
text: Browser SDK window.Genesis.action(id,data) sends an action. actions.get(id) and actions.list() describe current permissions. state.get() returns public state; state.subscribe(fn) receives updates. stage.get() returns presentation and anchor data. stage.point(event,element) returns normalized frame coordinates accounting for letterboxing. on('state',fn) receives the filtered view. The existing image, voice and character helpers depend on host support; the standalone reference player currently supports typed actions and standard text/click/choice controls. State subscriptions begin when the host supplies the first view. They receive the current view immediately when registered after that point. Initialize UI placeholders in HTML, and read player seats and game state inside a subscription. Custom interfaces execute inside opaque sandbox iframes with blocked network connections. The host remains responsible for essential exit, reconnect and billing UI. Host-message handling checks the frame source, nonce and declared action.

title: SDK API reference / Node host and adapters
heading: Node host and adapters
text: Node host and adapters Construct GenesisHost(sessionId,project,{storage,policy,services,providers}), then await initialize(). Methods: join, leave, view, action, playback, runJob, tick, retry and skip. diagnostics() is author-only and includes internal state. Never expose it to general participants. Providers implement id, paid, capabilities, start, poll and optional cancel. Start receives a stable idempotencyKey, a job and anchor. Poll returns running, ready or failed. Ready scene results include videoUrl and an actual end-frame imageUrl. Storage implements load/save snapshots. The reference host serializes per-session operations in one process; distributed hosts provide their own transaction/lease adapter.

title: SDK API reference / Custom tools
heading: Custom tools
text: Custom tools Request namespaced capabilities such as tool.lookup in the manifest. The host must independently grant the capability and register a provider with that capability. Controllers emit {id,type:"tool.request",toolId:"tool.lookup",data:{...}} . Arguments and returned result.data are bounded to 12 KB. Provider validate(job) rejects invalid arguments before paid authorization. Completion enters job.ready with event.data.data. Generic tools preserve the stage; the controller decides presentation. No provider credential or unrestricted fetch capability enters the sandbox. Collective submissions emit vote.cast with actorId and optionId. Controllers can inspect context.ballots to implement weights, quorum, early resolution or custom aggregation. Returning window:null closes the decision. The standard controller keeps deadline aggregation.

title: SDK API reference / Portable project boundary
heading: Portable project boundary
text: Portable project boundary The JSON Schema is exported as GENESIS_PROJECT_SCHEMA. createGenesisProjectManifest clears hosted package versions and saved-game connections without mutating the source definition. Inline source remains confined to transport projects. The Worldstreams editor preserves host references separately when applying manifest edits. definition.interface.chat optionally requests {presentation:"minimized"|"open"|"disabled",reactions:boolean} . Chat access and enforcement stay with the host. extensions uses namespaced keys such as org.example , up to 16 namespaces and 16 KB total. Unknown extension data is preserved without execution or capability grants.

title: SDK API reference / Participation version 1
heading: Participation version 1
text: Participation version 1 For explicitly claimed seats, declare definition.participation.seats as {version:1,slots:[{id,label}],queue:true,maxSeatsPerIdentity:1} . Seats require multiplayer mode and spectators, with minPlayers no greater than the slot count and slots no greater than maxPlayers. Slot IDs are unique. Defaults are queue false and one seat per verified identity. Configure room as shared or private; room discovery is implemented by the hosting adapter. Sequencer defaults seat worlds to one shared public arena per published version. Continuous worlds always share their audience room. Ordinary projects without seats retain their admission behavior. Genesis.players.get() and subscribe(fn) expose version, capabilities, seats with actorId/canClaim/canRelease, queueLength, own queuePosition/canQueue, and own cooldownUntil. claim(seatId) , leave(seatId) , joinQueue() and leaveQueue() request server transitions. A browser cannot specify another actor, a role, lease, identity, cooldown or removal authority. The host injects the verified identity. Sequencer requires sign-in to claim or queue. Watchers can remain anonymous. Controller context.participation contains public seats and queueLength, with no identities or credentials. Events are seat.claimed, seat.released, queue.joined and queue.left. To release a defeated player, return {id,type:"players.release",seatId,expectedActorId,cooldownMs:5000} . Expected ownership is checked before commit; the cooldown is limited to 60 seconds and follows the identity across new actor IDs. Replacements are promoted atomically from the e

title: SDK API reference / Structured LLM and asset helpers
heading: Structured LLM and asset helpers
text: Structured LLM and asset helpers Tool tool.llm.generate accepts {prompt,context?,responseSchema} with a bounded object schema. Completion emits job.ready with event.data.data. Effect guard {key,value} must match current server state before a result is applied; obsolete jobs emit job.cancelled without exposing their result. Controllers receive jobs metadata for scheduling, including status, type and guard. Genesis.assets.get(path) resolves host-provided media sources. Portable bundles use declared assets/ paths; Sequencer interfaces use asset:// IDs after attachment. importGenesisProjectBundle preserves complete assetFiles; importGenesisProjectArchive returns only the project for compatibility.

title: Architecture
heading: Architecture
text: Architecture Genesis is a portable runtime and project format. A world has a browser interface, a synchronous sandboxed server controller, accepted state and asynchronous host effects. The host owns authentication, provider credentials, permissions, spending, publication and storage. Sequencer implements that host with managed media, LLM requests, versioned assets and stream infrastructure. A universal World Model Context Protocol The GENESIS Context Engine connects structured world state, settings and player actions to your World Model. Its optional Visual Context component prepares starting and reference images, supplying image context directly alongside text context. The tinted LLM and World Model are external services connected through host adapters. Streaming delivery returns generated video to the player's interface. Scroll the diagram horizontally to explore the full loop. Use the GENESIS modules your project needs. Connect external models through host adapters. Visual Context Visual Context is the image-generation and reference-image flow inside the GENESIS Context Engine. A project can declare a boolean setting in definition.genesis.configSchema , then read it through context.config.settings to decide when its controller emits image.request . Declare the capability in the project and grant it on the host. The host adapter connects the image provider and enforces permis

heading: A universal World Model Context Protocol
text: A universal World Model Context Protocol The GENESIS Context Engine connects structured world state, settings and player actions to your World Model. Its optional Visual Context component prepares starting and reference images, supplying image context directly alongside text context. The tinted LLM and World Model are external services connected through host adapters. Streaming delivery returns generated video to the player's interface. Scroll the diagram horizontally to explore the full loop. Use the GENESIS modules your project needs. Connect external models through host adapters.

title: Architecture / Visual Context
heading: Visual Context
text: Visual Context Visual Context is the image-generation and reference-image flow inside the GENESIS Context Engine. A project can declare a boolean setting in definition.genesis.configSchema , then read it through context.config.settings to decide when its controller emits image.request . Declare the capability in the project and grant it on the host. The host adapter connects the image provider and enforces permissions and spending limits. The LLM can supply a bounded image prompt. Validate that reply, request the image and wait for job.ready before using its accepted image or anchor in the next scene request. Visual and text context then reach the World Model through its adapter. The adapter must support the image input your project uses.

title: Architecture / The action and generation loop
heading: The action and generation loop
text: The action and generation loop Copy Viewer action -> authenticated host -> controller -> committed state | bounded effect | provider / backend LLM | validated job.ready data | controller -> UI The same LLM service can return both a video prompt and structured scene facts. Validate the structured result before accepting it. A director describes the committed game outcome; it cannot rewrite health, payments or eligibility. A generated battle move set is installed once for its battle. The effect's guard cancels obsolete results after player replacement. A video result becomes playable only after an actual end-frame checkpoint. A live-direction receipt acknowledges queued delivery, not playback completion. One server worker advances each shared hosted session under a durable lease. Viewer reads return accepted state and renew throttled presence. They do not independently poll the provider. Cloud Tasks retries failures; a busy worker returns a retryable failure. Durable provider records and stable request IDs survive process loss. Ambiguous paid submissions require reconciliation instead of issuing another charge. These are scoped guarantees, not a promise of exactly-once behavior from arbitrary providers. SDK memory/file adapters support one host process. Distributed creators provide transactional storage, job admission and durable scheduling. Never run the loopback authoring server on the public internet. Host adapters validate capabilities independently of the project's requests. Relative paths identify portable assets. ZIP import enforces safe paths, supported media, declare

title: Hosting and authority
heading: Host authority
text: Host authority Creator code owns rules, scores, UI, turns, votes, story behavior and declared project settings. Manifest capabilities are requests. GenesisHostPolicy supplies independent host grants and ceilings; a manifest cannot raise them. The deployment owns authentication and actor admission, content policy, storage access, resource admission, billing, wallet state and verified purchases. GenesisHostServices exposes authorization and action-moderation hooks. GenesisMeteringAdapter describes authoritative viewer admission/release integration. A host calls these from its own viewer infrastructure, not from controller-provided times. Sequencer's shared hourly gem pool, split across active authenticated viewers, stays in its private host adapter. GenesisCommerceAdapter quotes registered offers and verifies platform receipts. No controller defines prices, adds gems or asserts that a purchase succeeded. Host quote/confirmation/charge infrastructure remains external. The portable preview does not implement a wallet or a commerce UI. Keep required billing, exit and reconnect controls outside creator iframes. Filter participant-private state and omit server state from view broadcasts. Public metadata and configuration are not secret storage. Diagnostics are restricted to authors/operators. The local runner binds loopback, issues actor tokens, checks same-origin writes, and rejects

title: Portable projects
heading: Project, product and host
text: Project, product and host Genesis is a portable project contract. It can run inside a hosting product or the standalone reference runner. Layer Owns Genesis project Metadata, assets, interface, controller, participation, action contracts, stream defaults, content preferences, requested capabilities and budgets. Hosting product Ownership, collaborators, publication/discovery, avatar account connections, chat membership/moderation, offers, prices and payouts. Host policy/services Credentials, model access, granted tools, resource ceilings, required safety checks, authoritative metering, wallets and verified receipts. Requested settings are validated independently of grants. Importing a project does not replace product permissions or grant new host capabilities. Unknown manifest fields are rejected. Namespaced extensions preserve bounded configuration and have no execution or permission semantics. Hosts can impose narrower limits. Worldstreams currently supports 100-character titles, 280-character listing descriptions and 14-second continuous stream chunks. Unsupported values are rejected before saving, while the portable project contract remains independent of those product limits. The three entry points are genesis.json, interface.html and controller.js. HTML may include browser JavaScript for local interactions. Shared world logic executes in the isolated controller. A viewer i

title: Compatibility
heading: Compatibility and growth
text: Compatibility and growth Genesis can continue to evolve after publication. Releases use semantic versioning. Project format 1, participation 1, bounded tool contracts and asset registry fields are versioned independently. Existing format-1 projects without assets or LLM capabilities remain valid. Unknown fields fail visibly; hosts advertise capabilities and supported cadence instead of silently promising unsupported behavior. Keep new provider integrations in adapters. Add optional capabilities before making a host depend on them. Extensions are bounded inert data and grant no authority. A host pins controller/interface versions for a session, and new drafts affect new sessions. Maintain supported version fixtures and round-trip tests. Breaking format changes require an explicit migration and a major release; do not mutate existing session rules halfway through a game. This source preview runs CI on Node 20 and 22 in sequencer-media/genesis . npm publication is disabled with private:true until an authorized package release. GitHub repository visibility is managed separately. Keep commercial account records, operational credentials and deployment settings outside the repository.

title: Authoring contract
heading: Authoring Genesis projects
text: Authoring Genesis projects When asked to build a world from an idea, use skills/create-world-stream/SKILL.md. Deliver a playable local project with its interface, controller and complete asset bundle. Use the nearest starter and preserve the user's chosen provider. Read docs/api.md and the appropriate example before editing. Author settings in genesis.json with interfaceFile and controllerFile references. Keep browser code in interface.html and shared rules in controller.js. Archive exports include the three entry files, their JSON Schema and complete declared media. Transport JSON can inline both sources. Keep product records and host authority outside the manifest; unknown fields are rejected. Keep HTML/CSS/browser JavaScript separate from the synchronous server onEvent controller. Use window.Genesis.action(actionId, data), actions.get(id).canSubmit, state.subscribe and stage.point in interface code. Declare each action and its typed fields. Controllers return public/private/server state, an eligible input window and effects. Asynchronous generation runs through host effects and returns job.ready or job.failed events. Determine committed game outcomes before requesting a generated scene. Generation does not verify visual correctness. Open actions only for eligible actors and use challenge IDs for timing games. Use the actual end-frame anchor for exploration and the saved star

title: Contributing
heading: Contributing
text: Contributing Use Node 20 or later. Run npm ci and npm test from this directory. Use the bug report or feature request forms to describe reproducible behavior or a concrete creator workflow. For a pull request, fork the repository, create a branch and keep the change focused. Include the relevant checks and an example when it introduces a new programming pattern. The documentation site is built from the Markdown guides, the README and the bundled authoring skill. Run npm run docs:build after editing them, or npm run docs:dev for a local browser preview. Commit the generated HTML with its source changes. The build checks local links and section anchors. Keep demos clearly labeled as recorded examples. The hosted site lives at sequencer.media/genesis . Check this deployment mode with npm run docs:build -- --out .genesis-site --base-path /genesis/ . Site navigation stays under that path; creation links reuse Sequencer's existing My Worlds editor and sign-in. Keep portable SDK examples available for creators using their own hosts. Keep the runtime independent of a deployment, provider or framework. Host adapters own credentials, identity, purchases, content policy and resource grants. Project manifests only request capabilities. A change to actions, controller context, state views, jobs or playback events needs a compatibility test and an API changelog entry. Add a runnable example

title: Security
heading: Security
text: Security Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to the maintainers through the repository's private vulnerability-reporting channel once the public repository exists. Until launch, use the private development channel. Never attach credentials or private user data to public issues. The controller has no network, Node or filesystem globals. Browser interfaces run in a sandbox. LLM input/output is bounded and validated as data. Host policies independently enforce tool grants, authenticated actor identity, spending and owned media. Creator projects cannot set gem rates or wallet balances. Paid live access requires server revocation, not just a short JWT expiry. Sequencer's current paid adapter requires LiveKit Cloud with participant token revocation; self-hosted LiveKit is rejected for this paid path. It issues a lease-scoped identity, stores revocation requests durably and removes expired or leaving viewers. Reactor startup tokens are withheld from paid public viewers until the protected native transport is ready. Cleanup is scheduled before revocation is attempted. If cleanup keeps failing for 30 seconds, the worker requests whole-room teardown. Billing refunds do not block that teardown.
